definition: Project signals — language, license, maintainer, maturity, docs, and packaging. The baseline of "is this a serious project we can rely on?".
Where the agent sessions physically runs, what dependencies are needed, and what each instance costs to start and keep alive.
First-party support for the chat surface: generative UI components, tool-call rendering primitives, streaming hooks
The HTTP surface exposed to clients: transport (SSE/WS), auth, tenant scoping, resume, cancel, partial tool args, and HITL approvals. Scores zero when the framework ships no server.
Concurrent session isolation, horizontal scaling across pods, background/scheduled jobs, and worker/queue models — readiness for many concurrent agents in production.
Session data model, built-in and pluggable stores, durable mid-run checkpointing, fork/branch, and deterministic replay.
The bare ReAct loop: tool dispatch, token streaming, turn boundaries, and in-process event emission.
Routing across LLM providers, per-task model selection, and sub-agent model overrides.
Levers over what the LLM sees: auto-compaction, lifecycle hooks, hook mutation/blocking power, prompt-cache optimization, and progressive disclosure of tool results.
Long-term cross-session memory, semantic recall, retrieval primitives, and knowledge ingestion — distinct from sessions because it survives across conversations.
Skills as a runtime primitive — a discoverable, versioned, tenant-scoped capability surface beyond raw tools. Scores high when the framework ships a SKILL.md-style loader.
Spawning child agents, passing context, isolating their state, and routing events back. Includes handoffs and team patterns.
Publish workflow, draft/active/deprecated lifecycle, versioning, RBAC, and content-addressable refs for skills, prompts, tools, and other shared assets.
Tool definition ergonomics, schema generation, error handling, sandboxing, and the breadth of built-in tools shipped with the framework.
Model Context Protocol integration — client, server, transport options, and how easily MCP servers plug into the agent surface.
Guardrails, content filters, policy hooks, integrity labels, and how the framework supports safety constraints across tool calls and outputs.
First-party tracing, span/event model, OTEL compatibility, third-party integrations, and what is visible by default vs needing instrumentation.
Typed run-loop context, server-controlled tenant/user fields, per-turn tool filtering, and forced-args mechanisms the LLM cannot see or override.
Eval datasets, replay harnesses, scoring primitives, regression detection, and CI hooks — whether the framework has a story for "does the agent still work after this change?".
Local dev server, hot reload, playground UI, scaffolding CLI, and the speed of the inner loop when iterating on prompts, tools, and skills.
